r: Literally dropping under the eaves of a house to listen: eaves + drop.
d: to secretly listen to a private conversation

r: Latin 'ebullire', to boil over: double l, then -ience.
d: cheerful, bubbly enthusiasm

r: Greek 'ek' (out of) + 'kentron' (center): two c's up front, off-center.
d: unconventional and slightly strange

r: Greek 'ek' + 'chymos' (juice): double c, then 'h', then 'y'.
d: a bruise; discoloration from blood leaking under the skin

r: Greek 'ekklesia', assembly or church: double c, then 'le-si-AS-ti-cal'.
d: relating to the Christian church or its clergy

r: Greek 'ekdysis', a getting out: 'c' then 'dy', with a 'y' in the middle.
d: the shedding of an outer skin, as by insects or snakes

r: French 'echelle', ladder: 'ch' sounds like 'sh', and it ends in -elon.
d: a level or rank in an organization

r: Greek 'echo' + 'lalia' (speech): keep the 'h', one l in each part.
d: the automatic repetition of another person's words

r: Greek 'eklektikos', selecting: one c at the start, then 'lec-tic'.
d: drawing on a wide variety of sources or styles

r: Greek 'ekstasis', standing outside oneself: it ends in -sy, not -cy.
d: an overwhelming feeling of great happiness

r: Greek 'oikoumene', the inhabited world: American spelling starts with plain 'ec'.
d: promoting unity among Christian churches; universal

r: Greek 'ekzein', to boil out: the 'cz' is the trap, sounding like 'gz' or 'ks'.
d: a condition in which patches of skin become itchy and inflamed

r: Latin 'edax', greedy (from 'edere', to eat, as in 'edible'): -cious ending.
d: greedy; devouring

r: German 'edel' (noble) + 'weiss' (white): 'ei' and a double s.
d: a small Alpine plant with woolly white flowers

r: Latin 'effervescere', to boil up: double f, then the 'sc' and -ent.
d: bubbly; vivacious and enthusiastic

r: From 'efficacy': double f, 'ica', then -cious.
d: successful in producing a desired result

r: Double f, then 'ci' for the 'sh' sound, as in 'sufficient'.
d: achieving maximum productivity with minimum waste

r: Latin 'efflorescere', to blossom: double f, a 'sc', then -ence.
d: the state of flowering; a peak of development

r: Latin 'effluere', to flow out: double f, then -uvium.
d: an unpleasant or harmful smell or discharge

r: French 'effronte', shameless: double f, then -ery.
d: insolent or impertinent behavior

r: Latin 'effulgere', to shine forth: double f, ends in -ent.
d: shining brightly; radiant

r: Latin 'e grege', out of the flock: 'gre-gious', with -ious.
d: outstandingly bad; shocking

r: It's 'eight' + 'h': the t stays, so there's an h on both sides of it.
d: constituting number eight in a sequence

r: Welsh 'session': 'ei', double d, then 'fod' (pronounced 'vod').
d: a Welsh festival of music, literature, and performance

r: Greek 'ek' (out) + 'phrasis' (speaking): a 'k' and a 'ph'.
d: a vivid literary description of a work of visual art

r: Greek 'eleemosyne', alms (source of 'alms'): double e, then -mosynary.
d: relating to or dependent on charity

r: From 'elegy': ele-GI-ac, the i before the a.
d: wistful or mournful, like an elegy

r: -ible, not -able, and an 'i' after the l: el-I-gible.
d: meeting the conditions to do or receive something

r: Latin 'e limine', out the threshold: one l, then 'i-mi'.
d: to completely remove or get rid of

r: Arabic 'al-iksir': ends in -ir, not -er.
d: a magical or medicinal potion

r: Greek 'elleipsis', omission: double l, single p, then -sis.
d: three dots showing that words have been left out

r: Latin 'eloqui', to speak out: one l, 'quence' with an e.
d: fluent, persuasive speaking or writing

r: Latin 'lucidus', clear (as in 'lucid'): e + lucid + ate.
d: to make something clear; to explain

r: Latin 'macies', leanness: one m up front, then 'ci' for the 'sh' sound.
d: abnormally thin or weak

r: Two r's and two s's: you go really red and smile shyly.
d: to make someone feel awkward or ashamed

r: Double z, then 'le' + 'ment': embezzle + ment.
d: theft of money entrusted to one's care

r: French 'bouche', mouth: em + bouch + ure.
d: the way a player applies the mouth to a wind instrument

r: Latin 'emittere', to send out: one m, double s, -ary.
d: a person sent on a special mission as a representative

r: Stress is on 'mit', so the t doubles before -ed. One m.
d: produced and sent out (light, gas, sound)

r: Latin 'mollis', soft: one m, double l, then -ient.
d: a substance that softens and soothes the skin

r: Unlike 'emollient', it has only one l: e-MOL-u-ment.
d: a salary, fee, or profit from employment

r: Ends in -or, like 'governor', and 'per' sits in the middle.
d: a sovereign ruler of an empire

r: Greek 'emphysan', to inflate: 'ph', then 'y', then -sema.
d: a lung disease causing breathlessness

r: Greek 'empyros', in fire: 'y' (not 'i'), then -ean.
d: the highest heaven; the sky

r: Greek 'enkaustikos', burned in (as in 'caustic'): en + caustic.
d: painting with pigments mixed with hot wax

r: Greek 'enkephalos' (brain) + -itis: 'c' then 'ph', and -itis not -itus.
d: inflammation of the brain

r: Spanish 'enchilar', to season with chili: en + chil + ada, one l.
d: a rolled tortilla with a filling, covered in chili sauce

r: Greek 'en' + 'cheir' (hand): a handbook. 'ch' sounds like 'k'.
d: a book of essential information; a handbook

r: Greek 'enkomion', praise: one m in the middle, -ium at the end.
d: a speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly

r: The 'e' of 'encumber' drops out: encumbR-ance.
d: a burden or impediment

r: Greek 'enkyklios paideia', all-round education: 'cyclo' + 'pedia'.
d: a reference work with articles on many subjects

r: 'ea' as in 'bread', and an American -or ending (British 'endeavour').
d: an attempt to achieve a goal

r: Greek 'endon' (within) + 'krinein' (to separate): ends in -crine.
d: relating to glands that release hormones into the blood

r: Latin 'enervare', to remove the sinews: one n. It means weaken, not energize!
d: to drain of energy or vitality

r: French 'enfiler', to thread on a string: one l, ends in -ade.
d: gunfire directed along a line from end to end; a suite of aligned rooms

r: Keep the 'e' of 'enforce' to keep the c soft: enforce + able.
d: able to be imposed or made effective

r: French 'enjamber', to stride over (jambe = leg): keep the silent 'b'.
d: the running on of a sentence from one line of poetry to the next

r: French 'boredom': double n, then 'ui'. Pronounced 'on-WEE'.
d: a feeling of listlessness and boredom

r: American spelling keeps both l's of 'enroll'; British uses 'enrolment'.
d: the act of officially joining a course, school, or list

r: en + 'sconce' (a small fort): an 'sc' and a 'c' for the s sounds.
d: to settle comfortably and securely

r: French 'together': ens + emble, with 'e' where you hear 'ah'.
d: a group of musicians or actors; a coordinated outfit

r: Greek 'enthymema', a thought: 'th', then 'y', then -meme.
d: an argument in which one premise is left unstated

r: Greek 'entomon', insect: ento-MOLOGY. Not 'etymology', the study of words.
d: the scientific study of insects

r: French 'entourer', to surround: en + tour + age.
d: a group of people attending an important person

r: French, from Italian 'capriola intrecciata': entre + chat, 'ch' as 'sh'.
d: a ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the legs repeatedly

r: French 'one who undertakes': entre + pre + neur. Don't drop the r after 'p'.
d: a person who starts and runs a business, taking on financial risk

r: Like 'pronunciation', the 'o' of 'announce' is gone: e-NUN-ciate.
d: to pronounce words clearly

r: It contains 'environ': environ + ment. Don't drop the n.
d: the surroundings or conditions in which a person or thing lives

r: Greek 'ephemeros', lasting a day: 'ph', then 'e-mer-al'.
d: lasting for a very short time

r: Greek 'ephemeris', diary: same start as 'ephemeral', ending in -is.
d: a table giving the positions of celestial bodies at given times

r: From the philosopher Epicurus: ends in -ean, not -ian.
d: devoted to sensual enjoyment, especially fine food and drink

r: Greek 'epi' (upon) + 'glottis': double t, -is.
d: the flap of cartilage that covers the windpipe when swallowing

r: Greek 'epiphaneia', manifestation: 'ph', then -any.
d: a moment of sudden and great revelation

r: Greek 'episkopos', overseer (source of 'bishop'): epi + scop + al.
d: relating to a bishop or bishops

r: Greek 'episteme', knowledge: epi-STEM-ology, with an 'e' after the t.
d: the branch of philosophy concerned with knowledge

r: Greek 'epistole', letter: silent t, ending in -tle like 'whistle'.
d: a letter, especially a formal or literary one

r: Greek 'epi' + 'thalamos' (bridal chamber): epi-tha-LA-mium.
d: a song or poem celebrating a marriage

r: Greek: ends in -e, said 'ee'. Rhymes with 'epiphany', not 'tome'.
d: a perfect example of a quality or type

r: Latin 'aequus' (even) + 'animus' (mind): equ + anim + ity.
d: calmness and composure, especially in difficult situations

r: Latin 'equus', horse: eques + trian, -ian at the end.
d: relating to horse riding

r: Latin 'aequus' (equal) + 'libra' (balance): one l, and -ium.
d: a state of balance

r: Latin 'aequinoctium': the x of 'equinox' becomes 'ct', then -ial.
d: relating to the equinox or the celestial equator

r: equip + ment: no 't' after the p and no double p.
d: the items needed for a particular purpose

r: equi (equal) + poise: keep the word 'poise' intact.
d: balance of forces or interests; a counterbalance

r: Stress is on 'quip', so the p doubles before -ed.
d: supplied with the necessary items

r: equi + valent (value): 'val' with an a, then -ent.
d: equal in value, amount, function, or meaning

r: Latin 'aequus' (equal) + 'vox' (voice): equi + voc + al.
d: open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous

r: German 'replacement': an 's' and then 'tz'.
d: made as an inferior substitute for something else

r: From 'error': double r, then -eous.
d: wrong; incorrect

r: Latin 'eructare', to belch: one r, then 'uc-ta-tion'.
d: the act of belching

r: Greek 'erythros' (red) + 'pella' (skin): 'y', then 'si-pe-las'.
d: a bacterial skin infection causing red patches
